questions.prompt: A Blob container has service SAS credentials bound to policy contractor-read. Other clients use a different policy and must keep working. Which action revokes the contractor group without rotating an account key?

options.explanation: The group's credentials lose their referenced server-side policy.
This is broader than requested and disrupts other key-signed clients.

options.text: Remove the contractors' Azure Reader roles.
options.explanation: These requests use a key-signed SAS, not their Azure Reader assignments.
An access tier does not revoke authorization.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Storage credential can reference a stored access policy on a blob container?

options.text: A service SAS for a blob in that container.
options.explanation: Service SAS supports the container's signed policy identifier.

options.text: An account SAS for Blob and Queue.
options.explanation: Account SAS does not support stored access policies.
User delegation SAS cannot reference this policy.

options.text: A Microsoft Entra OAuth access token.
options.explanation: OAuth authorization does not use SAS stored policy identifiers.

questions.prompt: An administrator tries to add a sixth stored access policy to a Blob container. The existing five policies must remain. Why does Azure reject the request?

options.text: The container supports at most five stored access policies.
options.explanation: The quota applies to policy entries per resource.

options.text: The account has already issued five SAS tokens.
options.explanation: Issued SAS count is not this policy quota.

options.text: The container contains more than five blobs.
options.explanation: Blob count does not control the stored-policy limit.

options.text: Only one stored policy is allowed per account key.
options.explanation: Policies are resource-scoped, not one entry per signing key.
